content: Green tea, also known as Camellia sinensis, has various pharmacological interactions and potential effects when consumed in combination with certain medications or substances. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Green tea and bortezomib: Green tea reduces the effectiveness of bortezomib. Patients undergoing treatment with bortezomib should avoid green tea. 2. Green tea and abciximab: Green tea may enhance the effects of abciximab through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Green tea and adenosine: Green tea decreases the effects of adenosine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Green tea and albuterol: Green tea may enhance the effects of albuterol due to pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination can increase central nervous system (CNS) stimulatory effects because of the caffeine content in green tea. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Green tea and alteplase: Green tea may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with alteplase. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Green tea and amphetamine: Green tea contains caffeine, a CNS stimulant, which may have additive effects when combined with amphetamines. Excessive CNS stimulation can occur. Caffeine should be avoided or used cautiously. 7. Green tea and anagrelide: Green tea may enhance the effects of anagrelide through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Green tea and antithrombin alfa/antithrombin III: Green tea may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with antithrombin agents. Caution is advised. 9. Green tea and arformoterol: Green tea may enhance the effects of arformoterol due to pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing CNS stimulatory effects because of caffeine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Green tea and argatroban: Green tea may increase the risk of bleeding when combined with argatroban. Caution is advised. 11. Green tea and aspirin (oral, rectal, or combination products): Green tea may enhance the effects of aspirin through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of bleeding. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Green tea and benzphetamine: Green tea contains caffeine, which may have additive CNS stimulatory effects when combined with benzphetamine.
